title: Refresh compliance one-pager templates (SOC 2, ISO alignment, data residency, encryption/KMS)
creator: Talia Benson
content:
Context
Enterprise deals are increasingly gated on security/compliance collateral. We have 4 one-pagers in flight (SOC 2 posture, ISO/27001 alignment, data residency & retention, encryption & KMS). The draft text exists in Drive, but the templates are inconsistent and don’t reflect current Redwood branding or the “what we do and don’t say” guidance. This ticket updates the design system for these one-pagers so GRC/SE/Sales can publish consistent, credible PDFs.

Goals
- Standardize layout and visual hierarchy across all compliance one-pagers.
- Make the documents skimmable for procurement/security reviewers (clear headings, control boundaries, “deployment mode” callouts).
- Ensure competitive-safe, non-overpromising structure (space for disclaimers, evidence gating notes, and scope language).
- Provide a template that is easy to maintain (swap sections, update dates/versions, export to PDF reliably).

Non-goals
- Authoring final compliance/security claims (owned by Security/GRC/PM). This ticket is purely template + component guidance.
- Adding new product claims/features.

Deliverables
1) Figma templates (4 variants) built on a shared component structure:
   - SOC 2 one-pager template
   - ISO/27001 alignment one-pager template
   - Data residency & retention one-pager template
   - Encryption & KMS one-pager template
2) Shared components + rules
   - Header block with document title, deployment mode badges (Hosted / Dedicated / Private), version + last reviewed fields
   - “What this covers” / “What this doesn’t cover” module
   - Proof points module with icons + short claims + footnote markers
   - Callout module for evidence request process (NDA required) + internal contact placeholder
   - Footer with confidentiality label, canonical link placeholder, and changelog pointer
3) Export-ready PDF settings guidance (page size, margins, typography rules, and “no overflow” checks)

Template structure (standard)
- Top header
  - Redwood Inference wordmark (small, left)
  - Document title (H1)
  - Right-side metadata: Version, Last reviewed, Owner
  - Optional confidentiality tag: “Customer-facing (non-confidential)” vs “Customer-facing (under NDA)” (text-only; no lock icon to avoid implying restricted evidence)
- Section 1: Overview (2–3 bullets)
  - Purpose statement tailored per one-pager
  - “Deployment modes” chips: Hosted / Dedicated / Private (chips appear only where relevant)
- Section 2: Key points (3–5 icon bullets)
  - Each bullet: short claim line + clarifier sub-line
  - Icon style: simple line icons (monochrome) to keep tone “enterprise + factual”
- Section 3: Details (two-column)
  - Left: “What we do” (capabilities, controls)
  - Right: “Shared responsibility” / “Customer responsibilities” where applicable (esp. Private)
- Section 4: Evidence & next steps
  - SOC 2 report availability note (under NDA) + how to request
  - Link slot for Confluence/portal canonical request process
- Footer
  - Canonical URL placeholder
  - “This document is a summary; contract terms/control scope is defined in the MSA/DPA and applicable exhibits.” (standard footer disclaimer)

Brand + typography
- Typeface: Inter (matches current Redwood docs/console)
- H1: 22–24pt / semibold; H2: 12–14pt / semibold; body: 10–11pt
- Use sentence case headings (avoid title case) to align with docs tone.
- Color: keep mostly black/gray text; Redwood green reserved for small accents (badges, section rule) to avoid “marketing brochure” vibe.
- Accessibility: ensure contrast > 4.5:1; avoid light gray body text.

Iconography
- Use a consistent set (outline, 1.5px stroke) with no filled shapes.
- Icon categories used across templates:
  - Shield/check (security program posture)
  - Key (encryption/KMS)
  - Globe/pin (residency)
  - Clock (retention)
  - Log/list (audit logging)
  - Users/lock (SSO/RBAC)
- Avoid icons implying certifications (e.g., “seal/badge”) for ISO alignment to reduce misinterpretation.

Content constraints baked into layout (to avoid overpromising)
- ISO page includes a dedicated “Alignment, not certification” callout zone (always visible).
- Data residency page includes a fixed “Region availability varies; confirm in deal context” callout slot.
- SOC 2 page includes a fixed “Report available under NDA; scope details in report” callout slot.
- Private deployment pages reserve space for shared responsibility boundary language.

Open questions resolved
- Page size: US Letter (primary) with an A4 auto-layout variant. Decision: ship Letter template; include A4 variant as secondary page in same Figma file for EMEA requests.
- “Badges” vs “tables” for Hosted/Dedicated/Private: use chips + a small 3-column mini-table only when needed (e.g., encryption key ownership differences).
- Footer confidentiality language: use neutral “Customer-facing summary” and reserve “Under NDA” only for evidence access sections, not the whole PDF (per Legal/Finance request).

Links
- Drive drafts (source text):
  - compliance-one-pager-soc2-draft (Google Drive)
  - compliance-one-pager-iso27001-alignment-draft (Google Drive)
  - compliance-one-pager-data-residency-draft (Google Drive)
  - compliance-one-pager-encryption-and-kms-draft (Google Drive)
- Messaging framework reference:
  - Confluence: security-and-trust-messaging-pillars
- Related design work:
  - DES-2924 (data flow diagram hosted vs private)

Review checklist
- Consistency: spacing, type scale, section naming, footer metadata fields
- Export: no text overflow at 100% zoom; PDF output legible when printed
- Tone: factual, non-promotional; avoids certification seals/claims
- Ready for content owners to paste approved language without reflowing the entire page

Acceptance criteria
- Four templates exist in Figma and share the same component library.
- A Sales/SE user can duplicate a template, paste updated approved text, update version/date fields, and export a single-page PDF without layout breakage.
- Templates include visible placeholder for last reviewed/owner + a consistent disclaimer footer.

Status
- Completed. Templates finalized in Figma and shared with Product Marketing + GRC for content insertion. Export tests completed for Letter; A4 variant added as a second frame.
comments: 2026-01-10 (Talia Benson): Creating this ticket to unblock publishing of the refreshed compliance one-pagers. Please prioritize “credibility + skimmability” over decorative visuals; customers are reading these like mini-control summaries.

2026-01-14 (Camila Reyes): Drafted initial layout grid + header/footer pattern. Proposed chip-style deployment mode badges and an evidence callout module. Sharing for early feedback from Soojin + Olga before we build all four variants.
2026-01-16 (Olga Petrov): Please include a permanent callout zone on ISO template that explicitly says alignment ≠ certification. We’ve had multiple RFPs misread prior collateral.
2026-01-18 (Soojin Lee): Agree on keeping it non-marketing. Avoid stamp/seal visuals. Add a small “What this covers / doesn’t cover” section to reduce follow-up questions and keep claims bounded.
2026-01-23 (Naomi Feldman): For Private, we need room for shared responsibility language. Please keep a consistent module that can expand by ~2 lines without breaking a one-page export.

2026-02-02 (Daniel Carter): SOC 2 template should reference ‘report available under NDA’ and not include any statement about audit opinion in the template itself (content will vary by audit period). Footer disclaimer is helpful.

2026-02-10 (Camila Reyes): Built all four variants using shared components. Added fixed callout areas: ISO alignment disclaimer, residency nuance, SOC 2 NDA/evidence request, Private shared responsibility. Added A4 variant frame for EMEA requests.

2026-02-18 (Markus Klein): Export looks good. The two-column details section is very scannable. Request: on encryption/KMS, keep an optional mini-table slot for key ownership boundaries (Hosted vs Private).
2026-02-26 (Camila Reyes): Finalized optional mini-table component and documented export settings. Marking Done; handing off to Talia/Olga/Soojin for final content paste + publish.
